mainTopic: Which of a wife's vows her husband can cancel (הפרה): vows of עינוי נפש versus vows about matters between him and her
overview: This amud opens by finishing an earlier argument: a wife who stops bathing will not drive her husband away, because 'a fox does not die from the dust of its own den.' The גמרא then brings a ברייתא supporting רב אדא בר אהבה. Vows of עינוי נפש can always be cancelled, while other vows can be cancelled only if they touch the relationship between husband and wife. The ברייתא gives examples of vows he can cancel, vows he cannot cancel, and vows he does not even need to cancel, and רבן גמליאל says he should cancel even those. The גמרא shows that this ברייתא fits רבי יוסי, who treats eye paint and rouge as marital matters. It then explains the case of a vow against intimacy using רב כהנא's rule: she cannot forbid herself to him, but she can forbid her own pleasure, and then he must cancel it. Next, a ברייתא about keeping strict customs, based on 'לא יחל דברו', is shown to follow רבן גמליאל. Finally, רבא asks רב נחמן whether, for the רבנן, a vow against intimacy is עינוי נפש or a marital matter. רב נחמן begins answering from a משנה, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A fox does not die in the dust of its own den
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the claim that a wife's vow not to bathe harms the marriage. A husband is used to his wife, just as a fox is used to the dust of its own den.
steps.simpleTranslation: For we have never found a fox that died from the dust of its own den.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is closing an earlier argument by rejecting the idea that a wife who does not bathe will become repulsive to her husband. It uses a short folk saying to make the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier claim was that not bathing is a 'between him and her' matter, because it could push the husband away. The answer is that a creature is never harmed by what it lives with every day. A husband who is used to his wife will not be put off just because she skipped bathing.

keyTerms.meaning: Fox
The dust or earth of a den or pit
We have not found; this never happens

phrases.english: For we have not found a fox
that died from the dust of its den.
phrases.notes: The den is the fox's own home. It is so used to that dust that the dust can't hurt it, and a husband is just as used to his wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁלֹּא מָצִינוּ שׁוּעָל שֶׁמֵּת בַּעֲפַר פִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the reasoning from the earlier part of the daf about a vow not to bathe.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that a wife not bathing counts as a 'between him and her' matter because it will repel the husband.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes the husband will be repelled, but a person is not put off by someone he is used to.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב אדא בר אהבה: the general rule
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that vows of עינוי נפש can be cancelled in every case. Other vows can be cancelled only when they concern matters between husband and wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא is taught in line with רב אדא בר אהבה. If her vows involve affliction, he can cancel them, whether they concern him and her or her and other people. If they do not involve affliction, he can cancel them when they concern him and her, but not when they concern her and other people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up the position of רב אדא בר אהבה from the earlier discussion. It lays out the two categories of vows a husband can cancel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate reasons a husband can cancel a vow. The first is עינוי נפש, meaning the vow makes her suffer. The second is דברים שבינו לבינה, meaning the vow affects their marriage. A vow of affliction can be cancelled even if it only concerns other people, but a vow without affliction needs the 'between him and her' reason.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא is taught that agrees with him
Self-affliction; a vow that causes her suffering
He cancels (the husband's power to undo his wife's vow)
Between him and her; matters affecting the marriage
Between her and other people

steps.whyThisMatters: This two-category framework (affliction vs. marital matters) is the backbone for deciding which of a wife's vows the husband may cancel.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: It is taught in accordance with Rav Adda bar Ahava:
Matters that involve affliction
he cancels, whether between him and her
or between her and others.
Those that do not involve affliction:
between him and her, he cancels.
Between her and others, he does not cancel.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the bathing argument to a ברייתא supporting רב אדא בר אהבה.
steps.raayaObject: The position of רב אדא בר אהבה from earlier in the sugya.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא splitting vows into affliction vows (always cancellable) and non-affliction vows (cancellable only between him and her).

steps.title: Examples: produce versus working for relatives and feeding animals
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains its rule with cases. A vow against eating produce can be cancelled. Vows not to work for relatives or feed the animals cannot be cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If she said, 'Produce is קונם for me,' he can cancel it. If she said, 'קונם that I will not work for my father,' or 'for your brother,' 'for your father,' 'for my brother,' or 'that I will not put straw before your animal or water before your cattle,' he cannot cancel it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks 'How so?' and gives concrete examples of the rule it just stated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not eating produce causes her suffering, so it is עינוי נפש and he can cancel it. Not working for relatives or not feeding animals causes her no suffering. The ברייתא treats these as matters between her and others, so he has no power over them.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? (introduces examples)
A vow formula that forbids something like a sacrifice
He may cancel
Straw (animal feed)

phrases.english: How so?
If she said: "Produce is konam for me"
he may cancel it.
"Konam that I will not work for my father,"
"for your brother," "for your father," "for my brother,"
or "that I will not put straw before your animal
and water before your cattle"
he cannot cancel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the general rule of the ברייתא with examples.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An affliction vow (produce) can be cancelled. Non-affliction vows about others (working for relatives, feeding animals) cannot.

steps.title: Eye paint, rouge, and intimacy: cancellable as marital matters
steps.stepSummary: Vows not to paint her eyes, not to wear rouge, or not to be intimate can be cancelled because they affect the marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'That I will not paint my eyes,' 'that I will not put on rouge,' or 'that I will not have marital relations': he may cancel these, because they are matters between him and her.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives examples of the second category: vows without affliction that he can still cancel because they touch the marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Skipping makeup does not make her suffer, so it is not עינוי נפש. But her appearance and their intimacy directly affect the husband. That makes these vows דברים שבינו לבינה, which he may cancel.

keyTerms.meaning: I will paint (my eyes with kohl)
I will apply rouge
I will have marital relations

phrases.english: "That I will not paint my eyes,"
"that I will not put on rouge,"
or "that I will not have marital relations"
he may cancel, because they are matters between him and her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the examples, now showing the 'between him and her' category.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Vows against eye paint, rouge, or intimacy can be cancelled as matters between husband and wife.

steps.title: Making his bed, mixing his cup, washing him: no need to cancel
steps.stepSummary: Vows refusing to make his bed, mix his drink, or wash his face, hands, and feet do not need to be cancelled at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'That I will not make your bed for you,' 'that I will not mix your cup for you,' or 'that I will not wash your face, hands, and feet for you': he does not need to cancel these.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a third group of vows that the husband does not even have to cancel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are personal services a wife does for her husband. The usual explanation is that she is already obligated to do them, so her vow cannot take effect in the first place. That is why no cancelling is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Make (spread) the bed
Mix the cup (dilute wine with water)
He does not need to cancel

steps.whatToRemember: Three groups of a wife's vows: affliction vows can always be cancelled. Non-affliction vows can be cancelled only if they affect the marriage. Vows refusing her duties toward him need no cancelling at all.
steps.confusionAlert: 'He does not need to cancel' is not the same as 'he cannot cancel.' Here the vow does not bind her anyway, while in step 3 the vow binds her and he has no power over it.

phrases.english: "That I will not make your bed for you,"
or "that I will not mix the cup for you,"
or "that I will not wash for you
your face, your hands, and your feet"
he does not need to cancel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third category to the examples: vows that need no cancelling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Vows refusing to make his bed, mix his cup, or wash him need not be cancelled.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל: he should cancel them anyway
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל says the husband should still cancel the vows that do not need cancelling, based on the פסוק 'He shall not profane his word.' A second reading of the same פסוק teaches that a חכם cannot release his own vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל says: he should cancel them, as it says, 'He shall not profane his word.' Another explanation: 'He shall not profane his word' teaches that a חכם cannot release his own vows.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with רבן גמליאל, who disagrees slightly with the last ruling. He says the husband should cancel those vows anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said vows like refusing to make his bed do not need to be cancelled. רבן גמליאל says the husband should cancel them anyway, because a person should not break his word, and a vow left standing might lead to that. The ברייתא then adds a separate lesson from the same פסוק: a חכם cannot release his own vows.

keyTerms.meaning: He should cancel (the vow)
He shall not profane his word, meaning he must not break what he said
Another explanation
Releases vows (what a חכם does)

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel says: he should cancel,
phrases.notes: He means the vows from the last step, like refusing to make his bed, which don't strictly need cancelling.

phrases.english: as it says: "He shall not profane his word."
Another explanation: "He shall not profane his word"

phrases.aramaic: מִכָּאן לְחָכָם שֶׁאֵין מַתִּיר נִדְרֵי עַצְמוֹ.
phrases.english: from here we learn that a sage cannot release his own vows.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא by adding רבן גמליאל's view on the vows from step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even vows that don't need cancelling should be cancelled, so that the word is not broken. A חכם cannot release his own vows.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that only רבי יוסי treats vows against painting the eyes and rouge as matters between husband and wife. The ברייתא cancels them for that very reason, so it follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the one we heard say that 'I will not paint my eyes' and 'I will not rouge' are matters between him and her? רבי יוסי. And the ברייתא teaches that he cancels them because they are matters between him and her.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the whole ברייתא has been quoted, the גמרא shows why it was brought. The ברייתא matches רבי יוסי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There was a question about how to understand רבי יוסי: are these vows of עינוי נפש or matters between husband and wife? The ברייתא clearly cancels painting and rouge because they are matters between him and her. That fits רבי יוסי as he was explained earlier, so it backs up that explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Whom have we heard (say this)?
I will paint my eyes (with eye makeup)
I will put on rouge
Matters between him and her, things that affect the marriage

phrases.english: Whom have we heard who said
that "I will not paint my eyes" and "I will not rouge"
are matters between him and her?
It is Rabbi Yosei.
And the baraita teaches that he can cancel
because they are matters between him and her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the lesson from the ברייתא that was just finished.
steps.raayaObject: The view that רבי יוסי treats vows against painting and rouge as matters between husband and wife.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא, which cancels these vows because they are matters between him and her.

steps.title: What case is the vow about intimacy?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's ruling that a vow not to be intimate can be cancelled. It asks what exact case this is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'And that I will not be intimate' can be cancelled because it is a matter between him and her. What is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to one line of the ברייתא and asks what exact situation it means. This sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vow about intimacy could be worded in different ways. The גמרא wants to know which wording the ברייתא has in mind, because the wording changes whether cancelling is even needed.

keyTerms.meaning: I will be intimate (with my husband)
What is the case? How do we picture it?

phrases.english: The Master said: "And that I will not be intimate"
he can cancel it because it is a matter between him and her.
What is the case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about one ruling in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Exactly how the wife worded the vow about intimacy.

steps.title: It can't mean she forbade herself to him
steps.stepSummary: Suppose she said, 'Benefit from intimacy with me is forbidden to you.' Then no cancelling is needed, because she is already obligated to him and cannot vow that away.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say she said, 'Benefit from intimacy with me is forbidden to you,' why do I need cancelling? She is obligated to him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a first explanation of the case and throws it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Through marriage, a wife is obligated to her husband for intimacy. A vow cannot remove something that already belongs to someone else, so a vow forbidding herself to him never takes effect. If so, the ברייתא would have no need to say he cancels it.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a first try that will be rejected)
Benefit from intimacy with me is forbidden to you
Obligated or bound (to him)
Cancelling a vow

phrases.english: If you say that she said:
"Benefit from intimacy with me is forbidden to you,"
why do I need cancelling?
She is obligated to him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries a first answer to the question in step 8 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading the ברייתא as a vow that forbids her to him.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That vow never takes effect, since she is already obligated to him, so cancelling would be pointless.

steps.title: She forbade herself from benefiting from him
steps.stepSummary: The case must be where she said, 'Benefit from intimacy with you is forbidden to me.' This fits רב כהנא's teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is where she said, 'Benefit from intimacy with you is forbidden to me,' and this follows רב כהנא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct case. The vow forbids her own pleasure, not his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the vow is about what she herself may enjoy. That is hers to forbid, so the vow does take effect, and the husband needs to cancel it. The גמרא says this fits רב כהנא and is about to quote him.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces the correct answer)
Benefit from intimacy with you is forbidden to me
And this follows רב כהנא

steps.confusionAlert: The two wordings differ by one letter: תשמישי (with me) versus תשמישך (with you). One forbids him, which doesn't work. The other forbids her, which does.

phrases.english: Rather, it is where she says:
"Benefit from intimacy with you is forbidden to me,"
and this follows Rav Kahana,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected case from step 9 with the correct one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא means she forbade herself from benefiting from him, which needs cancelling, as רב כהנא taught.

steps.title: רב כהנא's rule about the two wordings
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא rules that if she forbade herself to him, he can make her be intimate. If she forbade his intimacy to herself, he must cancel the vow, because we don't feed a person something forbidden to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: if she says 'Benefit from intimacy with me is forbidden to you,' he can make her be intimate with him. If she says 'Benefit from intimacy with you is forbidden to me,' he must cancel it, because we do not feed a person something that is forbidden to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רב כהנא, whose teaching backs up the answer just given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first wording the vow has no power, so he can simply make her keep her obligation. In the second, she really is forbidden to enjoy it, and she cannot be made to do something forbidden to her, just as we don't feed someone forbidden food. So the only way forward is for him to cancel the vow.

keyTerms.meaning: He can compel her
And she is intimate with him

keyTerms.term: אֵין מַאֲכִילִין אֶת הָאָדָם דָּבָר הָאָסוּר לוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: We do not feed a person something forbidden to him

steps.whatToRemember: A wife's vow cannot remove what she owes her husband, so forbidding herself to him does nothing. But she can forbid her own pleasure, and then he must cancel the vow, since she can't be made to do something forbidden to her.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key rule of vows: a person can forbid her own benefit, but cannot use a vow to take away what she already owes someone else.

phrases.english: For Rav Kahana said:
If she says "Benefit from intimacy with me is forbidden to you"
he can compel her and she is intimate with him.
If she says "Benefit from intimacy with you is forbidden to me," he must cancel it,
because we do not feed a person
phrases.notes: Feeding is a picture. She can't be made to do something her vow forbids her, just like you can't give someone forbidden food.

phrases.english: something that is forbidden to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the teaching that step 10 relied on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If she forbids herself to him, he can compel her. If she forbids his intimacy to herself, he must cancel the vow, since we do not feed a person something forbidden to him.

steps.title: Who taught the ברייתא about strict customs?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא and asks which תנא it follows. The ברייתא says a permitted thing that others treated as forbidden may not be treated as permitted. It also says a תלמיד חכם cannot undo his own vows. Both teachings come from 'לא יחל דברו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who taught this ברייתא? 'If something is permitted, but people got used to treating it as forbidden, you may not treat it as permitted and undo their custom. The פסוק says, "He shall not profane his word." Another explanation: "He shall not profane his word" teaches that a תלמיד חכם cannot undo his own vows.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא and asks whose opinion it is. This step sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats a strict custom as if it were a kind of vow, based on 'לא יחל דברו'. It then reads the same פסוק a second way: a sage cannot release his own vows. The גמרא wants to know which known opinion matches this approach.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (who taught this)?
Things that are permitted by the letter of the law
People took on the custom of treating them as forbidden
"He shall not profane his word": don't break what you committed to
A Torah scholar, someone able to release others' vows

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two meanings of the same פסוק. The first is about keeping a strict custom. The second is about a sage who cannot release his own vow. The words are the same, but the lessons are different.

phrases.english: Who taught that which is taught in a baraita:
Matters that are permitted
but others were used to treating them as forbidden

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה רַשַּׁאי לִנְהוֹג בָּהֶם הֶיתֵּר
phrases.english: you are not allowed to treat them as permitted
in a way that cancels their custom,
because it is said: "He shall not profane his word."
Another explanation: "He shall not profane his word"
from here we learn about a Torah scholar
that he cannot undo his own vows.
phrases.notes: A sage can release other people's vows, but he can't do that for his own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about the source of a ברייתא that uses the same פסוק and the same 'דבר אחר' found next to רבן גמליאל in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's opinion does this ברייתא follow?

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows רבן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is it? It is רבן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: this ברייתא matches רבן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6, רבן גמליאל used 'לא יחל דברו' to say a husband should cancel even a vow that does not truly take effect, and the same 'דבר אחר' about a sage's own vows followed. This ברייתא has the same pattern: it treats a strict custom as binding like a vow, even though it is not a real vow, so it matches רבן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose (opinion) is it?

phrases.english: Whose view is it?
It is Rabban Gamliel.

steps.title: רבא asks how to classify a vow against intimacy
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן about the view of the רבנן. Is a wife's vow against intimacy a vow of affliction (עינוי נפש), or a matter between husband and wife?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked רב נחמן: According to the רבנן, is marital intimacy a matter of affliction, or a matter between him and her?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a question. A husband can cancel two kinds of vows, and he wants to know which kind a vow against intimacy belongs to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband can cancel vows of עינוי נפש and vows of דברים שבינו לבינה. These are two different categories. רבא wants to know where a vow against intimacy fits according to the רבנן, the Sages who argue with רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (raised a question)
Marital intimacy
Affliction: a vow that makes a person suffer
Matters between husband and wife

phrases.english: Rava asked Rav Nachman:
Marital intimacy, according to the Rabbis,
is it a matter of affliction,
or a matter between him and her?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the topic of intimacy vows and asks how to classify them
steps.sheelahInformationSought: According to the רבנן, is a vow against intimacy עינוי נפש or דברים שבינו לבינה?

steps.title: רב נחמן begins to answer from a משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says the answer was already taught in a משנה. He quotes a woman who said, 'I am removed from the Jews.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You already learned it in the משנה: 'And I am removed from the Jews.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן starts answering by pointing to a משנה. The quote continues on the next amud, where he will draw his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of giving his own opinion, רב נחמן shows that a משנה already settles the question. The case is a woman who forbade her intimacy to all Jews. How the משנה treats that vow will show which category it belongs to.

keyTerms.meaning: You (already) learned it
'I am removed from the Jews': my intimacy is forbidden to all Jews

phrases.english: He said to him: You learned it:
"And I am removed from the Jews,"
phrases.notes: This quotes a woman's vow from a משנה (90b). She means her intimacy is forbidden to all Jews.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering רבא's question from step 14 by citing a משנה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer can be learned from the משנה of 'I am removed from the Jews'. The proof is completed on the next amud.
